column1: # Runtime CPU features the pinned engine detects, at revision
# b4e3a9056567ed8145fc4fa29850d6f1f261ac2b, and what a conforming platform
# probe must do about each one.
# This table, not any one crate's constant, is the declaration of the reported
# feature vocabulary. Both the Linux and the Windows probe assert their lists
# against it, which is what keeps two platform crates on the same architecture
# from drifting apart without a shared constant to hold them together. It lives
# under engine-linux/tests because that is where the coverage test runs; its
# subject is the engine, not Linux.
# COLUMNS
#   arch       the architecture whose vocabulary the row constrains
#   feature    the name as it appears in the engine's detection call
#   routing    what the engine does with the answer:
#                routes_by_default                selects a different kernel,
#                                                 with no environment key in
#                                                 the predicate, so a replica
#                                                 of this distribution can and
#                                                 does take both arms
#                routes_only_under_a_refused_key  selects a different kernel,
#                                                 but only when an environment
#                                                 key is set that the startup
#                                                 admission scan refuses AND
#                                                 that the engine's own
#                                                 execution planner does not
#                                                 write for itself at model
#                                                 load. Both halves are load-
#                                                 bearing: the planner sets and
#                                                 removes several dozen managed
#                                                 keys from detected host
#                                                 features long after the scan
#                                                 has run, so a key being
#                                                 refused to an operator says
#                                                 nothing on its own about
#                                                 whether a replica reaches the
#                                                 branch. No row is in this
#                                                 class at the current pin; the
#                                                 note on i8mm below is why the
#                                                 one that was is not.
#                reporting_only                   detected to be described, not
#                                                 to be branched on
#   published  what a probe must do:
#                required  MUST appear in that architecture's vocabulary
#                optional  MAY appear; recorded so a name that is published
#                          without a live gate carries its reason
#                no        MUST NOT appear
#   site       one representative source location at the pin, engine-relative.
#              Representative, not exhaustive: avx512bw alone is detected at six
#              sites in the engine's inference module, and a table citing one
#              site per feature reads as a smaller claim than it is making.
# The invariant tying the last two columns together is asserted, not assumed:
# routing=routes_by_default and published=required are the same set. Without
# that, a routed feature could be quietly demoted to `optional` to make the
# coverage assertion pass, which is the one edit that would make this file
# worse than no file.
# WHY `optional` EXISTS AT ALL. neon is published today and has no live gate:
# the engine detects it only to describe the host. Dropping it would shrink a
# string replicas already publish, retiring a live identity to tidy a list. It
# stays, with the reason in the table instead of in someone's memory, and if a
# pin bump gives it a live gate the routing column moves and the invariant above
# promotes it to required.
# WHY i8mm IS NOT `optional`. It was, and the classification was false. The gate
# at the site below is `env_flag_enabled("CAMELID_MAC_Q8_PREFILL_I8MM") &&
# is_aarch64_feature_detected!("i8mm")`, and the startup admission scan does
# refuse that key to an operator — but the engine's execution planner writes it
# "on" itself, from the same detected feature, whenever it plans a supported
# Apple-silicon Q8_0 row (engine src/execution_plan.rs:470-472, applied at
# src/api/mod.rs:6847). That write happens at model load, after the scan, which
# the lane's `apply_deterministic` documentation names as a structural limit of
# the startup gate rather than a gap to be closed there. So a stock replica does
# take the branch: two hosts differing only in i8mm run different prefill
# kernels once the row threshold is met, and under the old classification no
# probe was required to publish the name that tells them apart. Any future row
# whose predicate names an environment key has to be classified against the
# engine's managed-key list, not against this distribution's allow list alone.
# The routing column describes the engine, not any one platform crate's build.
# The i8mm gate is compiled only into the macOS aarch64 build, so a Linux or
# Windows aarch64 host does not reach it; this table is keyed by architecture,
# so `required` asks every aarch64 probe for the name anyway. That is the
# conservative direction. A probe that publishes a name nothing routes on where
# it runs costs one name in a string; a probe that omits one that does route
# costs the identity its whole purpose.
# The amx and avx_vnni rows are `no` for a different reason worth keeping
# visible: the engine reads them from the kernel's CPU flag file rather than
# from cpuid, and uses them only to describe the execution plan. They are in
# this table so that adding one to a probe fails a test that explains why,
# rather than silently widening the published identity with a name no kernel
# branches on.
# Regenerate at every engine pin bump by sweeping the engine tree for runtime
# feature-detection calls and classifying each site by what consumes it — the
# routing column cannot be derived from the call site alone, because the
# environment gate that makes a branch unreachable usually sits in the same
# predicate and the reporting-only calls look identical to the routing ones.
# Against a stale file the coverage test asserts about an engine nobody runs.
# arch
aarch64
aarch64
aarch64
